alex.ng: Heads up — after landing int3 quant for Mariner13B on the staging runner I'm seeing a subtle but consistent quality regression on summarization tests. FP16 -> int3 BLEU/ROUGE deltas look small, but factuality/safety check fails more often. Anyone seen a headwise bias after low-bit kernel swap?
priya: what quant recipe did you use? standard per-channel PTQ or the newer mixed-range int3 we tested?
ajex.ng: per-channel symmetric PTQ with clip thresholds from our quant-config v2. I also enabled the fast rotary kernel path from runtime-optim.
alex.ng: here's the convert command I used:
```bash
tools/convert_model --in mariner13b.fp16 --out mariner13b.int3 --quant int3 --clip-config quant-configs/v2.json --vocab-map scripts/map_vocab_from_marian.sh
```
jordan: two quick checks: did you remap the tokenizer IDs exactly? we've had off-by-one sentinel issues when the vocab script inserts BOS/EOS at top. Also which rotary implementation? headwise or fused head-permute?
alex.ng: used the map script that preserves original ids but gzip->mmap conversion maybe changed ordering. rotary path set to headwise-fused.
lena: can you paste a sample fail and the logits? quick diff between FP16 and int3 KV cache logits is useful. sometimes rotary scale gets multiplied differently causing head-level magnitude differences.
alev-bot: eval-bot: automated-eval report attached — summarization QA fail rate: fp16 3.1% -> int3 9.8%, avg token logprob delta -0.43. Per-head attention norm variance increased on heads 6/11.
ajex.ng: pasted logs (snip):
```
FP16 head6 attn_norm mean 0.0123
INT3 head6 attn_norm mean 0.0298
KV cache tokens look fine, token id distribution matches, but rotary phase angles show small per-head offset (~0.0009 rad) on later tokens.
```
priya: that phase offset smells like packing/order mismatch in the rotary matrix reshape. Did quant kernels reorder head dims to optimize memory?
jordan: runtime-optim v1.8 did a head-major reorder for fused kernels. If the tokenizer map changed token ordering, some embedding offsets + reorder could create cross-head leakage. We had a bug where proj order != rotary order.
lena: try two experiments: (1) run with the fallback scalar rotary kernel (no head reorder) to see if regression disappears, (2) run a synthetic test forcing rotary phase to zero and compare rank of attn outputs.
alex.ng: running fallback now on a small 100-example suite. will post numbers.
priya: also try re-running conversion without gzip->mmap step (direct binary write) — mapping layer has produced subtle index remaps before.
alev-bot: eval-bot: fallback rotary run finished — fail rate drops to 3.6%, token logprob delta -0.05. Looks like rotary/fused kernel interaction is the culprit.
jordan: that's a smoking gun. likely kernel assumes contiguous head layout and our conversion added a padding stride per-head. We should add a conversion sanity check that verifies reshape invariants: expected layout (N,H,head_dim) contiguous, and compare a small random projection before and after conversion.
lena: I'll open a PR with a conversion test harness. alex, can you share the exact converted binary (sha256) and the fast-kernel build id? I'll repro locally.
alex.ng: sha256: b3f2e9d4... build-id: runtime-optim@1.8.2+gpuopt. Uploaded to s3://redwood-staging/mariner/int3/b3f2e9d4.bin
priya: note for release notes — don't enable fused rotary by default for int3 until we validate layout invariants across conversion tools. add a warning in optimizer.
sre-bot: deploy-bot: created ticket INF-4219 for kernel-layout-sanity-checks.
alex.ng: thanks — will follow up with diffs and a short triage doc. :thumbsup:
